torso_lean.source: ACE Seated Lat Pulldown: "Lean back slightly (no more than a 30 degree angle), using your legs to support your body (low back)"; -15 is a conservative mid-point kept well inside that 30-degree cap, matching the production doc's canonical lat pulldown example

scap_depress_cm.source: ACE Seated Lat Pulldown: "Depress and retract your scapulae (pull shoulders back and down) and attempt to hold this position throughout the exercise"; Physio-pedia Scapulohumeral Rhythm for the depression mechanics

muscles.peakSource: ACE Seated Lat Pulldown: pull the bar down driving the elbows towards the sides of the torso; lat effort is highest through that full-pull position, at the top of the hold

mistake.name: Lean and heave

tells.text: The torso swings back past the braced lean to heave the bar down.
The shoulders creep up before the pull finishes, ending it early.

mistake.source: ACE Seated Lat Pulldown (lean no more than 30 degrees, hold scapular depression throughout) and Physio-pedia Scapulohumeral Rhythm: swinging the torso past the braced lean and losing scapular depression before the elbows finish both hand the pull to momentum and the upper traps instead of the lats

machine.source: ACE Seated Lat Pulldown: reach up to grasp the bar with the arms extended overhead, which is a high pulley position

sources: Contact fact (D-FG7 (l), pulldown grip width): overhand, about 1.5x shoulder width on a wide bar, per the production doc's canonical lat pulldown example (docs/FORM-GUIDE-PRODUCTION.md doc:79)
